studyTargets.description: Solve 3 malloc/free exercises and pointer offset logic.

flashcards.frontQuestion: What does the unary operator `*` do when applied to a pointer variable in C?
flashcards.backAnswer: Dereferencing operator: accesses the value stored at the memory address pointed to by the pointer (e.g., `*ptr = 20;`).
No. Standard C strictly passes ALL arguments by value. To simulate reference semantics, C passes pointer values (memory addresses) by value.

flashcards.frontQuestion: What is the difference between malloc() and calloc() in stdlib.h?
flashcards.backAnswer: malloc(size) allocates uninitialized memory (contains garbage values); calloc(num, size) allocates memory and initializes all bytes to zero.

flashcards.frontQuestion: What is the arrow operator (->) used for in C?
flashcards.backAnswer: Member access through a pointer to a struct or union. `ptr->member` is shorthand for `(*ptr).member`.

flashcards.frontQuestion: Why does an array name decay into a pointer in most expressions?
flashcards.backAnswer: In C, an array identifier automatically evaluates to a pointer to its first element (&arr[0]), except with sizeof, &arr, or string literals.
